item.title: The 2024 Seahawks did indeed have one specific Michigan influence
item.description: The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
The story of the day on Tuesday featured the unexpected disclosure of a behind-the-scenes beef between the Seahawks and Broncos. And while the whole thing was eye opening (and likely not intended for air), one specific line caught my eye.

Regarding Broncos coach Sean Payton's assertion that the Seahawks had obtained training-camp footage through improper means, Macdonald said, "He thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant."

That's a reference to the 2023 Connor Stalions scandal in Ann Arbor, where Stalions developed a mechanism (in violation of NCAA rules) to scout future opponents with the goal of figuring out their sideline signals. In this specific context, Payton presumably suggested that the Seahawks sent someone to Broncos training camp to record their plays.

Beyond the fact that Macdonald's journey included a year on Jim Harbaugh's Michigan staff (2021, as defensive coordinator), the 2024 Seahawks employed former Michigan assistant Matt Weiss as an outside consultant. And while Weiss's coaching career has imploded due to criminal allegations of widespread hacking, it's fair to point out that the 2024 Seahawks had a distinct Michigan component.

That's not to say Payton's allegations had any merit. Faced with a threat that the Seahawks would sue the Broncos if Payton went public with his suspicions of shenanigans, the issue died. And it would have remained unknown if Macdonald had spoken about it into a hot mic.

It will be interesting to hear what Macdonald and Payton have to say about it today, when they meet with reporters for their usual Wednesday press conferences. Regardless of their likely efforts to downplay the situation and move on, the Seahawks have self-applied the kind of scarlet letter that will give the coaches of the teams they beat the same kind of excuse that plagued the Patriots during their run of dominance.

Pressed by owners as to why the Seahawks keep beating their teams, coaches can resort to the notion that the Seahawks cheat. Even without a shred of evidence to support that claim.

If/when that happens, it will trace to the fact that Macdonald got way too comfortable — and said way too much about a topic that otherwise would have never come to light.

Meanwhile, the Broncos host the Seahawks in 22 days, for a Thursday night game. Which will create a motivation for multiple media outles to fully explore the rabbit hole that, as of Tuesday morning, no one even knew existed.

item.title: Jaxson Dart injury is ‘not an ACL’, but the timeline still isn’t good: Report
item.description: NY Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart doesn't have a torn ACL, but is that good news?
item.content:encoded:
There hasn’t been much in the way of good regarding the injury to New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart.

At first it was believed that Dart only suffered an MCL strain when he was sandwiched between a pair of Los Angeles Rams defenders and could return inside of a month.

It was then revealed Tuesday morning that an MRI revealed that his injury is worse than initially believed. The reporting hasn’t revealed the exact nature of the injury, but that Dart would be out indefinitely and season-ending surgery is on the table.

That catches us up to Wednesday morning, when Mike Garafolo reported that Dart’s injury doesn’t involve his ACL.

Garafolo said:

“Ian Rapoport and I were both told yesterday, this is not an ACL. But, the MRI did tell a different story from what the Giants were initially expecting. There is more damage than what the evaluations on site showed.“

The Giants’ hesitancy to confirm the nature of the injury makes sense in the light of Garafolo and Rapoport’s reporting. ACL injuries are usually quickly confirmed and the recovery timelines are well understood.

A different or complicated injury could be good news, worse news, or just bad news depending on what the continuing tests and opinions show.

Garafolo added that Dart’s recovery could follow several different timelines depending on the exact nature of the injury. None of the potential timelines are “very good”, according to Garafolo, and Dart’s season being over remains on the table.

“There are a lot of people involved. That means inside doctors [inside the Giants organization], outside doctors, that means Dart, the Giants. Everybody is going to come together and make a collective decision.”

Dart, obviously, will lobby to take the quickest route back to the field. Dart is an incredibly competitive young man and even played through a high ankle sprain his final season at Ole Miss. However, that might not be best for his long term health. Garafolo says,

“A lot of times when you have a young player, particularly at the quarterback position, these decisions are made with the long term interest of the player in mind.”

The Giants had to take Dart’s uniform away from him after he tried to talk his way back onto the field Monday night. With that in mind, the Giants may need to protect Dart from himself as much as deal with his injury.

Garafolo ends by saying that we should expect clarity on Dart’s status and timeline in the coming days.

We’ll update with more as we get it.

item.title: For the Eagles, first down has been the worst down
item.description: It’s bad. Real bad.
item.content:encoded:
The new look Eagles offense hasn’t been much fun. There are multiple reasons, but one of them is that on 1st down, they’re terrible.

The offense is 28th in EPA/play and 31st in both yards per play and success rate; and have gained a 1st down on 1st down just twice, the fewest in the league. Oddly, neither were on 1st and 10, Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception in the 4th quarter against the Titans was on 1st and 17 , and then his TD on 1st and goal was from the 3.

On 1st down, the Eagles have as many negative plays as they do plays that gained 7+ yards, 9 each. On their 48 1st downs, they have failed to gain yardage on 18 of them. Their average 2nd down needs 8.7 yards to gain a first down, 26th so far this season.

They’re bad at everything. 

Though the Eagles run 65% of the time on 1st down. They stink there.

  • 24th in EPA/play
  • 27th in success rate
  • 28th in yards per carry

When the Eagles do throw on 1st down, they’re woefully short.

  • CPOE: 19th
  • EPA per play: 26th
  • Success rate: 31st
  • Air yards per attempt: 31st
  • Yards per attempt: 32nd

This is not a Jalen Hurts issue. He had the 5th highest air yards per attempt on 1st down in 2025, and 14th in 2024. 

Nor is this a lack of AJ Brown issue, he was 48th in air yards per target last season, nor is this a Dontayvion Wicks as his replacement issue, he was 56th.

And though it has only been two games, this isn’t a situation where one bad game, the team’s failure to gain a single 1st down on 1st down against the Commanders, is bogging down the numbers. The Eagles converted a 1st down on just 2 of 28 1st downs against the Titans, 7.1%. Given the same rate against the Commanders, the Eagles would still be dead last in 1st conversion rate on 1st down. The next worst team, the Steelers, have converted at 7.4%.

This is an offensive line and coaching issue. The Eagles are 19th in sack rate per play, and 28th in pressures per play. Short throws to beat the pressure is a tried and true way of masking offensive line problems, but the Eagles entire first down offense is throwing short passes. They’re not trying to take a shot down the field. Even Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception on 1st and 17 was caught 5 yards beyond the line of scrimmage, though he wasn’t the first read, that was a good progression by Jalen Hurts.

Two games is a small sample size, but the NFL is built out of small sample sizes. Two games is a playoff run. Two games into the season and the Bucs, Chargers, Colts, and Texans are in trouble.

Two games into the season and the Eagles offense is in trouble too. Moving Cam Jurgens, who co-leads the league in holding penalties, to guard didn’t improve things. Perhaps more time will result in improved offensive line play, but there’s not a rich history of teams making significant changes to their line in-season and getting great results.

item.title: Ravens sign former Raiders WR Sheldrick Jackson to practice squad
item.description: The Ravens added a former Bengals and Raiders wide receiver to their practice squad on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Ravens signed former Bengals and Raiders wide reciver Shedrick Jackson to their practice squad on Tuesday, per the NFL’s daily personnel notice.

Jackson, 26, will add depth to a Ravens wide receiver room that will be without third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane for at least three more games as he recovers from surgery on his fractured risk. Zay Flowers also missed Sunday’s loss to the Saints due to a hamstring injury. He practiced last Friday in a (very) limited capacity, and questionable field conditions for Baltimore’s upcoming trip to Brazil could sideline him in Week 3.

Originally a 2023 undrafted free agent, Jackson signed with the Bengals as a rookie and appeared in five games during the regular season. All but 5 of his 43 snaps came on special teams. He left Cincinnati early in the 2024 season and later landed in Las Vegas.

Last year, Jackson appeared in five games for the Raiders. Across 29 offensive snaps, he caught four of his five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown (plus a three-yard rush); on special teams, he played 39 snaps with one tackle.

The Ravens had an open spot on their practice squad after a flurry of moves that featured the addition of wide reciever Gage Larvadain and the re-signings of cornerbacks Lardarius Webb Jr. and Amani Oruwariye, among other moves.

Fun fact: Jackson is not related to Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson, but he is the great-nephew of former Heisman Trophy winner and NFL Pro Bowler Bo Jackson. e

item.title: Seahawks Week 3 power rankings: Seahawks stay atop the mountain thanks to Drew Lock
item.description: Winning on a consistent basis can make a team’s power rankings quite static.
item.content:encoded:
Entering Week 2, the national media was very high on the Seattle Seahawks, even despite them losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold to a glute injury. Now, after handily defeating the Arizona Cardinals, one would expect the national media to remain high on Seattle. Or will the victories of other Super Bowl contending teams (like the Buffalo Bills or Los Angeles Rams) potentially knock the Seahawks off a peg? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (BR), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle.

Starting with ESPN, the only site (of these five) who don’t have Seattle ranked at number one. ESPN ranks Seattle the second best team in the NFL, the same ranking as last week. In their ranking ESPN credits Drew Lock as “one of the NFL’s best backup QBs.” ESPN further notes that since stepping in for an injured Darnold, Lock has “completed almost 73% of his passes, with four touchdowns, zero turnovers, and only two sacks.” Additionally, Lock’s total QBR of 86.4 currently ranks fourth best in the league. The only team ranked above the Seahawks for ESPN? The Buffalo Bills. 

CBS Sports and PFT both also credit Lock’s performance as they keep the Seahawks ranked as the number one team in the NFL. CBS Sports notes that a good team is one that can “go on the road and win with a backup quarterback.” Just as Seattle did last week in Arizona. PFT meanwhile summed up the Seahawks performance with a simple “No Darnold? No problem.” 

NFL.com, who also kept Seattle ranked as first, noted that Lock’s impressive performance should allow Seahawk fans to worry less about the absence of Darnold. B/R, who also have Seattle ranked as the number one team in the NFL, also noted that Lock’s performance should allow the team to not feel rushed to get Darnold back to the field.

As you have probably noticed, the power rankings – and the reasoning behind their rankings are all pretty cut and paste from all of the polled national media sites. That can be the case when your team is not only the Super Bowl defending champion, but also one of the favorites to win the next Super Bowl. In these moments, power rankings can become very static. As is the case this week. All five of the above national media sites kept the Seahawks at the same ranking as last week. Entering week two, the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.2. Entering Week 3, the same 1.2 average remains. 

However, this is still the NFL. And despite being an overwhelming top ranked team by the national media, the Seahawks are only one loss (or even one poor performance) away from slipping down these rankings once again. Their next test comes against the Washington Commanders – quarterbacked by Marcus Mariota.

item.title: Is Pete Werner emerging as a key piece of Saints defense?
item.description: With Week 2 of the 2026 season in the books, let’s take at one of the stars of the game for New Orleans.
item.content:encoded:
New Orleans Saints linebacker Pete Werner entered the 2026 season with a bigger role potentially waiting for him.

For the first time in his career, Werner is playing without Demario Davis beside him. After spending years alongside one of the most important leaders on the Saints’ defense, Werner now has an opportunity to establish himself as one of the veteran leaders of the unit alongside Kaden Elliss.

Through two games, he is making the most of that opportunity.

Werner delivered an impressive performance in Sunday’s 24-17 win over the Baltimore Ravens, finishing with team-high 11 total tackles, including eight solo tackles. He also recorded a sack, three total pressures, a tackle for loss and a defensive stop.

His impact as a pass rusher was particularly encouraging, as he earned a 79.6 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus.

Werner’s performance came at an important time for New Orleans. The Saints trailed 14-3 at one point during the game, but the defense settled down and played a major role in helping complete the comeback. Baltimore managed just three points after halftime as New Orleans flipped the game.

Werner was consistently around the football throughout the afternoon. Much like he was in the season opener agains the Detroit Lions.

So far, he has shown that he is capable of taking on the increased responsibility. His ability to contribute against the run while also making an impact as a pass rusher gives New Orleans another versatile piece to build around.

It is still early, but Werner is off to a strong start in his sixth season and looks to be drifting away from the inconsistency that plagued the early years of his career.

The Saints may no longer have his mentor beside him, but Werner is showing that he is ready for breakout season.

item.title: Detroit Lions mailbag: What shakeups are coming on defense?
item.description: What changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense? We discuss on the latest mailbag podcast.
item.content:encoded:
Changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense.

After giving up the second-most points through two weeks and having an extended weekend to diagnose their problems, Lions coach Dan Campbell promised changes were coming.

“We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said Monday. “We’re going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and shake it up a little bit. And because they’ve earned that, we’ve got some guys in here that have earned some play time that they deserve a chance to do more for us.”

On top of that, the Lions have to make some adjustments in the secondary after losing starting safety Avonte Maddox for the season to a foot injury. They started by signing Jalen Mills to the practice squad and poaching rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald, but more mixing and matching is certainly on the way.

On this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast, Erik Schlitt and I offer ideas and depth chart shakeups the Lions may consider moving forward.

Our discussion starts at safety, where the Lions have some choices to make. Will the Lions roll with Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper as starters, or will Christian Izien take over one of those roles? Schlitt suggests the Lions may have a three-person rotation at safety moving forward.

But if the Lions pull Izien from the nickel position, how will that impact the cornerback room? Will Roger McCreary become the full-time starter, or will rookie Keith Abney see more opportunities? If it’s McCreary, then the domino effect continues at outside cornerback. Who is CB3? Is this where Ennis Rakestraw or Nick Whiteside get the call-up to the game-day roster? And is Rock Ya-Sin’s starting job in jeopardy?

That conversation kicks off this week’s podcast, but there are plenty of topics we cover this week, including:

  • Is it practical to simplify the defense right now?
  • Why does the defense keep looking good in training camp, but fail to carry it over to the regular season?
  • Are safeties more important than cornerbacks in this defense?
  • Is Brad Holmes to blame for early extensions that have backfired because of injury (Kerby Joseph, Alim McNeill)?
  • Does Kelvin Sheppard need a senior defensive assistant?
  • What’s more likely: Campbell fires Sheppard midseason, the Lions hire a defensive assistant, or Detroit rides out the season and reassesses in 2027?
  • Why does Dan Campbell have such a short leash on offensive coordinators, but leeway for Aaron Glenn and Sheppard?
  • When, if ever, will the Lions get offensive weapon reserves (Jacob Saylors, Tay Martin, Tom Kennedy) involved in the offense?

item.title: Week 3 matchup with Packers is a homecoming of sorts for Falcons’ Za’Darius Smith
item.description: Smith has played at Lambeau Field as an opponent once before, though he had little impact in a big Packers win.
item.content:encoded:
The 2019 offseason was a busy one for Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In his second offseason at the helm of the franchise’s personnel department, Gutekunst headed into the start of free agency with a plan: spend money to bolster a few position groups in desperate need of help, most significantly the edge defenders.

Gutekunst did just that, first agreeing to a 4-year deal with former Washington Commander Preston Smith before landing one of the biggest fish in the pond: Za’Darius Smith, who had spent his first four NFL seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.

The Smith Brothers proved to be a formidable tandem for the next two seasons. Za’Darius recorded back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns in 2019 and 2020, as he posted 13.5 and 12.5 sacks in the two seasons, respectively. Preston also had a double-digit sack season in the players’ first year in Green Bay with 12, though he tapered back a bit with just four in 2020.

The 2021 season brought an abrupt end to the experiment, however. A back injury and controversy about not being voted a team captain led to Za’Darius playing in just one game, the season opener, before being shut down on injured reserve. Green Bay released him in the offseason before the last year of his 4-year contract, and he signed with the Minnesota Vikings, where he posted another ten-sack Pro Bowl season. Since then, Smith has bounced around to various teams, spending time with the Browns, Lions, and Eagles before landing in Atlanta this offseason.

With a limited workload through two games with the Falcons, Smith has flashed some of the power rushing ability that made him a Pro Bowler in Green Bay and elsewhere earlier in his career. He has 2.5 sacks in just 44 defensive snaps so far this season, making him the only player on the Falcons’ roster with more than a half-sack so far this season despite being third among the team’s defensive ends in snaps. Two of those sacks came against his old teammate Aaron Rodgers in Week 1; meanwhile, Pro Football Reference has him down for a total of six QB pressures, certainly a solid rate to start the season.

Thursday night’s game will be Smith’s fourth time matching up with the Packers since his split with the team after the 2021 season, though only one of the previous three games took place at Lambeau Field. That came right away in 2022 with the Vikings, though Smith had little impact with just three tackles in a 41-17 Packers victory late in the season. Smith’s other two games also both came as a divisional opponent — the Vikings defeated the Packers in Minnesota in week 1 of that 2022 season, and Smith was a member of the Detroit Lions in 2024 when they beat Green Bay 34-31 at Ford Field on Thursday Night Football. Both of those two games saw Smith record a sack.

With starting end Samson Ebukam limited on the Falcons’ injury report this week, Smith might well be in line for a heavier workload. His snap count increased from 16 against the Steelers in Week 1 to 28 last Sunday against the Panthers. If Ebukam is significantly limited or inactive on Thursday, Smith will almost certainly be on the field for more than 30 snaps, and the Packers will need to find a way to cobble together a pass rush plan to minimize his impact on the game.

item.title: Jonathon Brooks to miss at least 6 weeks with core injury, marking yet another injury-riddled season
item.description: Jonathon Brooks has played in just five games since he was drafted in 2024.
item.content:encoded:
The Carolina Panthers thought they were getting a steal when the team selected running back Jonathon Brooks in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft. During his final season at Texas, Brooks looked like a massive talent, and was on his way to being the top-ranked running back in the draft before tearing his ACL.

That proved to be a harbinger of what was to come for Brooks. Injuries have come to define his career in the NFL, as Brooks will miss at least the next six weeks due to core-muscle surgery, according to NFL Network.

#Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks, who left Sunday’s win early, is expected to have surgery today to repair a core muscle injury that will land him on Injured Reserve, sources say.

Brooks is out at least 6 weeks, but should return with plenty of time to contribute down the stretch. pic.twitter.com/RvXTRINyMf

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 23, 2026

Brooks' college ACL injury led to the runner missing the Panthers' first 10 games during his rookie season. He made his NFL debut in Week 12, and was given a sprinkling of snaps over his first two games before drawing a start in his third NFL game. His appearance lasted just one carry, as Brooks again tore the ACL in his right knee.

After missing the entire 2025 NFL season, Brooks was expected to be finally healthy heading into training camp in 2026. He received plenty of offseason buzz, with some expecting him to challenge Chuba Hubbard for the lead role in Carolina.

Though a late groin injury threatened Brooks' availability before the season, he was able to get back on the field and play in Week 1. His playing time was limited, as he touched the ball just five times against the Chicago Bears.

Brooks received a similar workload in Week 2, touching the ball six times before leaving the contest after reaggravating his groin injury.

With the injury, Brooks has now played in just five NFL games since being drafted by the team in 2024. He has 18 career carries for 52 yards and has caught five balls for 66 yards.

Brooks was placed on injured reserve Wednesday ahead of his surgery, per ESPN. He’ll need to miss at least four games with the move. With Brooks down multiple weeks, the Panthers will work out veteran Austin Ekeler to see if he can be a possible replacement.

Though Brooks hasn't been a major contributor, the Panthers are off to a strong start in 2026. After losing in Week 1 to the Bears, the Panthers bounced back with an impressive win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2. Quarterback Bryce Young appears to have taken a step forward and Hubbard looks reinvigorated after an injury-riddled 2025.

The core muscle surgery isn't expected to keep Brooks out for the entire season, offering some hope he can still return and be a useful weapon for the team down the stretch. Given Brooks' injury history, though, it's tough to count on him staying on the field once he's ready to return.

Following the placement of Charlie Kolar and David Njoku on injured reserve this week, the Chargers are signing former Dolphins and 49er tight end Hayden Rucci to the active roster. He will join Oronde Gadsden II as the only two tight ends on the Chargers roster as of Wednesday morning.

Rucci played his collegiate football at Wisconsin where he caught 17 career passes for 200 yards and one touchdown. At the NFL Combine, Rucci measured in at 6’5 and 247 pounds. He ran his 40 in 5.04 seconds, jumped 32 inches in the vertical, and had a short shuttle time of 4.40.

In four career games played (all in 2025 with the Dolphins), Rucci played 39 total snaps. Most of those came as a run blocker (29) where he finished with an overall season run block grade of 56.6.

item.title: Brandin Cooks back in the NFC West
item.description: Brandin Cooks signs with NFC West rival and more NFL news on a Wednesday
item.content:encoded:
Brandin Cooks was drafted in 2014 by the New Orleans Saints and at this point, Cooks is a veteran journeyman of the NFL. He’s play for the Saints, the New England Patriots, the Los Angeles Rams, the Houston Texans, the Dallas Cowboys, the Buffalo Bills (any teams I missed?), and he’s now signing to the San Francisco 49ers practice squad.

For Cooks and the Rams, it was a fairly successful stint. Heck, had he and the Rams won the Super Bowl in the 2018 season, Cooks may have been the MVP with over 100 receiving yards. Had Jared Goff and Cooks connected on a touchdown, who knows? Maybe Cooks spends more time with the Rams than he did. Maybe Goff does too.

But the past can’t be changed, and instead, the Rams didn’t win that Super Bowl, Cooks seemed to get hurt often, and though Cooks was a solid Ram, he’s not likely to go down as an all-time great Ram.

That being said. Cooks has put together a solid if not great NFL career in terms of production, longevity and as far I am aware he’s a drama free type player. There’s a lot to like about Cooks, and the 49ers are giving him a chance to compete in 2026.

With the way the 49ers are looking right now who’s to say, maybe Cooks finds himself in another Super Bowl. We’ll see.

Source: Niners signing veteran receiver Cooks to practice squad (espn.com)

“Free agent wide receiver Brandin Cooks is signing with the San Francisco 49ers‘ practice squad, initially to get up to speed for games, a source told ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Tuesday.

Cooks, 32, joins a Niners team that has lost wideouts Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson to injury this season. Meanwhile, veteran wide receiver Mike Evans will need to be managed this week with a hip injury.

Cooks was the 20th pick in the 2014 draft by the Saints out of Oregon State, and he spent the first three years of his career with New Orleans. He returned to the Saints in 2025 but was waived in November after he requested his release. Cooks then joined the Buffalo Bills for the remainder of the campaign”

item.title: Woman says she warned 49ers about fake player scam months before arrest
item.description: A woman says she reported an alleged 49ers impersonator to the team last December. Daejon Love was arrested in August and charged with wire fraud.
item.content:encoded:
A woman says she contacted the San Francisco 49ers last year to report that someone was impersonating a player and that she was a victim of his scams.

According to a report from ESPN.com, Gwen Herndon said she contacted the 49ers on Dec. 20, 2025, via a "complaint/concern" form. Her message said that "there is a federal investigation surrounding a man pretending to be a 49ers player."

The man, 35-year-old Daejon Love, was named in the complaint, and Herndon added that Love stole money from her and that he was "severely damaging the reputation of your team."

"It was apparent to me that there were so many victims and there were going to continue to be victims unless a public statement was made and was very visible," Herndon told ESPN. "I knew that based on how fast he was moving."

Herndon received a response from the team's general guest services account on Dec. 27, stating they take "reports of individuals misrepresenting themselves as members of the San Francisco 49ers very seriously," and they couldn't comment on investigations of specific people.

Herndon sued Love in Oregon small claims court last year, alleging that she gave Love $10,000 for a property investment idea. When she asked for her money back, Herndon said Love blocked communication with her.

Love and 18-year-old Taylor Chan, 18 were arrested last month at the Boise, Idaho airport by the FBI and charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud.

Federal authorities say that Love and Chan created fictitious investments to defraud numerous women in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California, with Love meeting most of the women on the Internet through dating apps. Authorities say he defrauded more than 20 women out of approximately $1.3 million.

Last week, the FBI said 35 more women have said they were scammed by Love and Chan, bringing the total number of alleged victims to more than 60.

"We were surprised how many people were victimized in such a short period of time and then to have that many more come forward," Portland FBI Special Agent in Charge Doug Olson said at a news conference. "It's a large volume for just a couple of subjects. Our concern is that this fraud could be replicated by other individuals that are out there victimizing other people in similar schemes."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Woman says she warned 49ers about fake player scam months before arrest

item.title: Green Bay Packers News: Defense holding up its end of the bargain
item.description: The Packers’ defense has been getting the job done in the first two weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Through two weeks, the Packers’ have, generally speaking, not been good.

The offense is scattershot, held back by its abysmal offensive line. The wide receivers are dropping passes (though the rain had something to do with that), Jordan Love looks consistently spooked, and the running backs can’t find their way to the few (very few) holes being opened for them.

The defense, however! The defense has been very good. Reliable, even exciting at times — and that’s without Micah Parsons, their very best player. 

It’s to the point where I’m actually excited to see the Packers on defense. Well, maybe not excited, because it usually means the Packers have just wrapped up another disappointing offensive series. 

But still! Lukas Van Ness is doing cool things. Edgerrin Cooper is doing cool things. Evan Williams is doing cool things. Jonathan Gannon is conjuring blitzes that produce free runners at the quarterback. It’s delightful to see, and it’s keeping the Packers in games.

I don’t expect the Falcons’ pitiable offense will be the combo breaker here. The Packers will have a chance to do even more cool things on defense this week. It may not be enough to save their season, but it’s enough to at least keep things interesting.

item.title: John Harbaugh gets another chance to consider Colin Kaepernick
item.description: When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say.
item.content:encoded:
When Colin Kaepernick was being ignored by the NFL teams, he didn't have much to say. Now that he's selling a book, interviews with Kaepernick are popping up everywhere.

We haven't paid much attention to his various sit-downs and sound bites because, frankly, it's an old story. The NFL has long since moved on from Kaepernick, freezing him out long enough to make it unrealistic that the now-38-year-old quarterback would have a plausible path to a roster, a practice squad, or even a tryout.

Still, one news item caught our eye in recent weeks. With Kaepernick's book tour putting him back in the vicinity of the front burner, Giants coach John Harbaugh told Ian O'Connor of The Athletic that Harbaugh wanted to add Kaepernick to the Ravens in 2017.

Through it all, Kaepernick got one workout, five years ago with the Raiders. With the Giants now desperate for quarterback help (and with Jake Haener and Brandon Allen as the most viable options behind new starter Jameis Winston), why not bring Kaepernick in for a look?

Kaepernick continues to say that he's staying in shape, and that he wants to play. It should be immediately obvious whether he still has the abilities that made Harbaugh interested in him nine years ago.

Harbaugh's New York staff includes Greg Roman, who was the offensive coordinator during Kaepernick's first four years in San Francisco. It would be easy, in theory, to configure the offense to fit Kaepernick. If Kaepernick still has the skills he had when he last played.

It starts with a workout (and quite possibly ends with one). There's no reason not to give it a whirl. The anthem controversy has subsided. (Harbaugh and the Giants surely would want assurances that Kaepernick wouldn't dust it off, if he ended up on the sideline before games.)

The threshold question is how does Kaepernick look? And there's only one way to find out. The Giants, who now face not having Jaxson Dart for up to the rest of the season, have plenty of reasons to give Kaepernick a chance to show them what he can do.

It would be different if John Harbaugh hadn't recently spoken in such glowing terms about Kaepernick. With not many viable options available in free agency — and with Harbaugh having considerable power in New York — let's see if Harbaugh puts his recent words into current action.

item.title: The Falcons’ quarterback plan has become a four-alarm fire
item.description: Michael Penix Jr. gets another chance to make sense of Atlanta’s increasingly bizarre quarterback saga — or send the franchise searching for yet another answer.
item.content:encoded:
There’s something thrilling, in a nerve-wracking sense, about seeing a poker player down to their last chip, gambling on one final hand, hoping that at long last the cards will turn in their favor. Now, you know how this usually ends — that last chip vanishes, the player’s hopes and bankroll busted — but there’s always hope. 

We’re just two weeks into the 2026 season, and the Atlanta Falcons are already down to their last chip. Where other teams are still working out the last of the preseason aches and pains, the Atlanta Falcons are on their fourth — fourth! — named quarterback, as Michael Penix Jr. will start for the team this Thursday night against Green Bay. 

The Falcons embody Hemingway’s famous line about how bankruptcy happens: gradually, then suddenly. We are very much in the “suddenly” phase now with Atlanta, but the “gradually” phase began back in March 2024, when Atlanta signed Kirk Cousins to a four-year, $180 million contract. For about four weeks, it seemed like the Falcons had at last found their franchise replacement for retired local legend Matt Ryan. 

We should have known something was up, karmically speaking, when the Falcons were immediately accused of, and later fined $250,000 for, tampering during the Cousins signing process. And Cousins didn’t even get the chance to dispel those bad vibes with his play; just weeks after finalizing that massive deal, the Falcons drafted Penix. 

Not only did Atlanta fail to notify Cousins, which doesn’t seem like the optimal way to begin a relationship, but the Falcons bypassed more than half a dozen future Pro Bowlers, on both sides of the ball, to select the already-often-injured Penix. 

Diagnosing what happened from there — Penix and Cousins shuttling in and out of the starting job as each struggled with injury and/or ineffectiveness — is like reading a police report on the wreck that totaled your car. The Why and How don’t really much matter anymore; the real question now is, what to do from here? 

Another famous American philosopher, John Madden, has a notable line of his own: When you have two quarterbacks, you have none. To which the 2026 Falcons replied: Yes, but what if we have FOUR quarterbacks? 

Penix has been sidelined since November of last year with a torn ACL. Atlanta signed Tua Tagovailoa on a cheap one-year prove-it deal; Tagovailoa promptly suffered a oblique injury days after being named the Week 1 starter, and still hasn’t played. QB3 Cooper Rush has struggled so badly that Atlanta has exactly as many red zone possessions this year as you do. Fan favorite Jack Strand finally got the nod during Sunday’s blowout loss to Carolina, and on his very first NFL play, this happened: 

JACK STRAND'S FIRST NFL PASS IS A PICK-SIX 🥴

Strand entered the game for Cooper Rush who was benched.

(via @Panthers) pic.twitter.com/ogBkj9Atg5

— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 20, 2026

The last Falcon to throw a pick-six on his first play was a guy named Brett Favre … but he wasn’t a Falcon for much longer after that. 

The maddening aspect of all this chaos, for long-suffering Falcons fans, is that Atlanta has all the other pieces of a playoff-quality team already in place. Swap in a Baker Mayfield or a Jalen Hurts or half a dozen other quarterbacks in the 10th-to-20th-ranked range to run an offense with Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts et. al., and Atlanta instantly becomes a postseason contender. But it doesn’t matter how sweet your Ferrari’s  interior, sound system and tires are if you’ve got a lawnmower engine under the hood. 

And so the frustrations continue. Atlanta hasn’t reached the playoffs since the 2017 season, the second-longest drought, after the Jets, in the NFL. Even in the woeful NFC South, where there’s a home playoff game awaiting any team that manages to rise to the level of mediocre, Atlanta hasn’t been able to break through. 

The 2027 NFL Draft promises a wealth of quarterback talent, from Arch Manning to Dante Moore to whichever Fernando Mendoza-esque shooting star separates from the pack over the next 10 weeks. (‘Sup, Drew Mestemaker.) 

This puts the Falcons in an uncomfortable limbo: If Penix plays poorly, the Falcons can console themselves and their fans that there’s potentially a better option awaiting in the draft. If Penix plays with poise, precision and — most importantly — durability that he hasn’t shown yet, the Falcons might be able to salvage something from this 30-month debacle. 

But what about the most likely scenario — the possibility that Penix plays well enough to win a few games, not enough to win the division but enough to push Atlanta down out of the elite-QB draft slots? Do the Falcons attempt to go for a sixth quarterback in two-plus seasons? 

These are interesting times in Atlanta, the same way it’s interesting to be an overmatched quarterback with an NFL-quality defensive line chasing you. No matter what happens next under center for Atlanta, starting Thursday against the Packers, it’s going to be memorable … one way or another.

item.title: Adam Vinatieri sets Guinness World Record for highest field goal at over 11,000 feet above sea level
item.description: Vinatieri's trip to the Swiss Alps was part of promoting the Patriots' November game in Munich, Germany.
item.content:encoded:
Adam Vinatieri isn't a stranger to kicking in snowy conditions. But in the Swiss Alps? That was a first for the Hall of Fame kicker this week as he set a Guinness World Record.

On Tuesday, the 53-year-old Vinatieri set the record for kicking the highest field goal in the world at 11,332 feet above sea level at Jungfraujoch, also known as the "Top of Europe."

The conditions were a little more difficult than what he experienced at Foxboro Stadium during the 2001 AFC Divisional Playoff Game against the Oakland Raiders when he kicked a 45-yard field goal to send the New England Patriots to the AFC Championship Game.

.@adamvinatieri officially holds the Guinness World Record for the highest altitude field goal kick 🦵🙌

→ https://t.co/ssu3cepnxOpic.twitter.com/cSSPVd9Ty3

— New England Patriots (@Patriots) September 22, 2026

"Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots," Vinatieri said in a team release. "But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever seen in the NFL. You feel the altitude with every breath you take, your heart rate is different, your rhythm is different, and no one can really tell you beforehand how it will affect the kick, because no one has done this before. The fact that we were able to set the record under these conditions makes me very proud. This is definitely one of the most special field goals I've ever made."

The record attempt was part of the Patriots' promotion for their Nov. 15 game in Munich, Germany, against the Detroit Lions. The team holds market rights in the DACH region of Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

Vinatieri played 24 NFL seasons with the Patriots and Indianapolis Colts. He is the NFL's all-time leading scorer (2,673 points) and is the league record holder for field goals made (599), playoff points (238) and successful overtime field goals (12).

A three-time first-team All-Pro, Vinatieri won three Super Bowls with the Patriots and one more with the Colts. In Super Bowls XXXVI and XXXVIII, it was his foot that kicked the Patriots to championships in the final seconds. His on-field success led to him being part of the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2026.

item.title: Giants-Titans storylines: Moving on without Jaxson Dart
item.description: All of the optimism surrounding the 2026 Giants is gone. What will take its place?
item.content:encoded:
Jaxson Dart is likely not going to be under center for any of them, but the New York Giants still have 15 games to play in the 2026 NFL season. How will they do without their young quarterback, who played like a star in an impressive Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys?

We begin to find out Sunday at MetLife Stadium when the Tennessee Dabolls — er, Titans — come to East Rutherford, N.J. for a 1 p.m. matchup. Below are some of the storylines for the week.

Winning without Dart

The latest reporting from NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo is that “there are a few timelines on the table, none of them very good, one of them season-ending” for the Giants quarterback.

While we await word on that, it is obvious Dart will not play Sunday against Tennessee. And the Giants will be without him for the foreseeable future.

How will the Giants fare without Dart, especially if he is out all season? It is possible that John Harbaugh and his veteran coaching staff squeeze every ounce of juice from this imperfect Giants’ roster and they finish in the neighborhood of .500. It is also possible that a four- or five-win season, the kind of disastrous year the Giants figured was off the table due to Harbaugh’s presence, is back on the table.

Beginning with the 0-2 Titans, the Giants have a three-game stretch of games that should be winnable.

Tennessee is a young, winless team coming to MetLife Stadium. They did, though, put a Week 2 scare into the Philadelphia Eagles. The 1-1 Arizona Cardinals come to MetLife in Week 4. They are expected to be one of the league’s weaker teams. The Giants visit the 0-2 Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Commanders could be without star quarterback Jayden Daniels, who suffered his second dislocated left elbow in as many seasons on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys.

If the Giants cannot win at least two of those three games, another long, miserable, losing season could follow.

Harbaugh, one of the winningest head coaches of all time, is going to be challenged over the next 15 games.

The veteran head coach promised on Tuesday that the Giants will “be fighting every step of the way.”

“We haven’t even come close – not even close — to playing as well as we’re capable of playing as a football team,” Harbaugh said. “So, that’s really going to be the focus. I mean, it’s going to be something we’re going to have to, you deal with all the different challenges that you face and all the different adversity that you face, for sure. And even the prosperity, you learned that last week, you faced some of the prosperity, and prosperity sometimes can be more dangerous than adversity.

“All these challenges to put your best effort out there, play your best football, so you can win a football game. And we’re going to do that. These guys are going to do that. That’s what you get excited about. The prospect of our team playing the best football that they can play. And that’s what we’re working on, working as hard as we can, working like crazy as a football team to do that all together.”

The Giants referred to Dart’s injury as an in-game “gut punch.” Harbaugh does not expect that to cause a long-term letdown.

“The guys want to go win. They want to go play,” Harbaugh said. “Guys play. They’ll play. They play for each other. They play for themselves. They play for their families. They play because they believe they can win the game. And it’s never one person, never one person that wins or loses a football game. It’s everybody. And the more good players you can have out there, the better chance you’re going to have. There’s no doubt about it. But you still have to be a complete team to win games.

“If you get punched in the gut, are you going down? Are you going down? Are you going to crumple to the ground, as Jack Harbaugh would say, like a sack of sour apples and just fall to the ground and just rot away and wither away into the dust. Is that what you’re going to do?”

To win games, the Giants are going to have to accomplish several things:

  • They will have to get better play from quarterback Jameis Winston than the miserable 11 of 27 for 11 yards and an interception performance he gave them Monday night.
  • They will have to find some way to get explosive plays from their offense. The longest non-Dart run they have in two games is a 13-yard carry by Cam Skattebo. They have one pass completion of more than 20 yards, a 33-yard grab by Darnell Mooney.
  • The pass rush will have to remember that the regular season has started.
  • They will need to find a way to cover some of the league’s best receivers.
  • They need to hope that injuries to stars Brian Burns, Andrew Thomas, and Malik Nabers aren’t severe. Oh, and that other injuries don’t continue to pile up.

We begin to find out how life after Dart will go Sunday against Tennessee.

More injuries to worry about

Dart suffered the worst and most significant injury on Monday night. Still, the game against the Rams saw several other significant injuries to Giants stars.

  • Edge defender Brian Burns, who had a career-high 16.5 sacks last season, suffered a sprained left ankle.
  • Left tackle Andrew Thomas apparently suffered a groin injury on the Giants’ final offensive possession.
  • Wide receiver Malik Nabers left the game briefly with a shoulder injury. He had just one catch for 1 yard in the game.
  • Cornerback Deonte Banks missed Monday’s game with a calf injury. His status for Week 3 is unclear.

The initial injury report of the week comes out Wednesday afternoon. We find out more about the severity of these injuries then. With a short week before playing the Titans, it is fair to wonder just how short-handed the Giants are going to be in a game that not long ago looked like one the Giants should win.

Remember the Titans

This game has been circled on the calendar for a while simply because of the volume of former Giants — especially key Giants — who are now part of the Titans’ organization.

  • Daboll, fired last season as Giants head coach, is now running the Tennessee offense. Daboll, of course, was instrumental in the Giants’ decision to trade up last season to draft Dart.
  • Robinson is second on the Titans with six receptions for 47 yards, just 7.8 yards per catch. He had the only 1,000-yard season of his career with the Giants last season.
  • Bellinger has just one catch in two games, one of which he started.
  • Schlottmann has started both Tennessee games at center. Through two games, Schlottmann’s Pro Football and Sports Network ‘Impact Score’ is 72.6. For the Giants, starting center John Michael Schmitz is at 73.6. Both scores are slightly below what PFSN considers league average, a score of 75.0.

Where’s the pass rush?

The Giants’ defense was supposed to be built around what they hoped would be a dominant pass rush.

Burns is coming off a career-best season. Abdul Carter was drafted No. 3 overall in hopes he would be a game-wrecking pass rusher. He looked in the summer like he was about to fulfill that promise. Kayvon Thibodeaux has at times been a good, but not great, pass rusher. No. 5 overall pick Arvell Reese is an inside linebacker with pass rush potential. Interior defensive linemen Chauncey Golston and Darius Alexander have pass rush ability. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s defense used creative schemes to pressure Giants’ quarterbacks throughout training camp.

Through two weeks of the regular season, none of that talent, potential, and summer promise has mattered. The pass rush has been non-existent.

  • The Giants have one quarterback sack. Per NextGenStats, their 1.4% sack rate is 31st in the league. Only the woeful Miami Dolphins, who do not have a sack yet, are worse.
  • The Giants’ pressure rate of 26.1, again per NGS, is the worst in the league. The ball is coming out quickly against New York, with the 2.69-second time to throw against the Giants 26th overall. That is .41 seconds faster than league average. Still, the pressure rate isn’t good enough.
  • Against the Rams, the Giants’ pressure rate was even worse:
  • The “Get-Off” time for Giants defensive linemen — the time is takes for them to cross the line of scrimmage — is worst in the league at .94 seconds. If the ball is coming out quickly, and your linemen are getting off the ball slowly, that is a bad combination.
  • The Giants are giving up +.41 Expected Points Added (EPA) per pass play. Only the Dolphins are worse.

We knew entering the season that the Giants’ pass rush was going to have to cover for a questionable secondary. So far, it has not not.

That needs to change. Quickly.

item.title: Jeffery Simmons is still dominant for the Titans
item.description: Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons is still as dominant as ever through two weeks.
item.content:encoded:
There was chatter going around about Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons after Week 1. The Titans endured a lifeless performance versus the New York Jets, and Simmons didn’t pop enough. Well, it’s clear after Week 2 that he’s still a dominant defender.

Simmons leads the entire NFL in pass-rush wins through two weeks, according to ESPN Stats & Info. The Pro Bowl defender has been credited with 19 wins as a pass rusher. No contender has more than 15, with Minnesota Vikings EDGE Dallas Turner currently ranking second.

Simmons’ pass-rush-win-rate stands at 37%. Only New England Patriots DT Christian Barmore has a slightly higher win rate at 38%, because Simmons has played more reps. Not a single edge rusher in the NFL currently matches Simmons’ 37% win rate.

Pro Football Focus’ metrics largely agree. They have Simmons tied for first among defensive tackles in pressures with nine. His PFF win% of 17.7 percent ranks fifth among DTs, but none of the four interior defenders ahead of him have played as many reps as he has (Aaron Donald is in first after making his Week 2 debut with just 19 pass-rushing snaps. Simmons has 66).

Simmons dominated an Eagles offensive line in Week 2 that had Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall starting in prominent roles. Kendall replaced the injured Landon Dickerson. He had absolutely no answer for Simmons.

There was some concern that Simmons would take time to adjust to Robert Saleh’s new attack-style defense. Those whispers grew after Week 1 when fans believed Simmons’ impact was muted versus the Jets. This clearly isn’t the case at all.

Simmons is as dominant as ever. Every advanced metric (across different outlets) proves it. The Titans still have a superstar defensive tackle in Jeffery Simmons. Hopefully the rest of the defense catches up soon.

item.title: Eagles News: “Dontayvion Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal”
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/23/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles) has been a pretty good pickup; he’s looking like a real solid WR2 to pair with DeVonta Smith as WR1. Seems to me like Smitty and Makai Lemon missing a lot of time in training camp really helped Jalen Hurts foster a better connection with Wicks since that was often his top option to throw to. Good job by Howie Roseman to trade for Wicks on the cheap (two Day 3 draft picks) and sign him to an extension to keep him under team control through 2027.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Cam Jurgens’ fit, Dontayvion Wicks’ emergence, Zach Ertz’s role: Eagles thoughts – The Athletic

The passing game has exceeded what I expected, and the wide receivers are quieting any external concerns. Dontayvion Wicks is validating the summer optimism. One point I made frequently this offseason was that the Eagles didn’t need to replace A.J. Brown; DeVonta Smith could handle that No. 1 role. They needed to replace Smith as the No. 2 option. Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal when they acquired him via trade and signed him to a contract extension. Wicks has caught seven of 10 targets for 147 yards. All seven of his receptions have resulted in first downs or touchdowns. His average depth of target has been 15.7 yards. Three of his receptions have traveled over 20 yards in the air. Four of his five receptions Sunday were on third down, and two were for third-and-12 conversions. Hurts trusts him. Wicks runs precise routes. He makes difficult catches. Wicks and Smith have combined for 20 catches for 317 yards through two games. That’s more yards than in any of the first two games Brown and Smith played together. This doesn’t mean the Eagles have a duo like Brown and Smith, but it’s a formidable combination.

Eagles-Titans Film Review: A very good offense is hiding in here – BGN

The Eagles won 24-20, and I came away feeling much better about the passing game than I did after Week 1. The Eagles found answers against the Titans’ coverage, attacked the weaknesses I flagged in my preview (which is always great to see), and repeatedly converted third-and-long. However, the offense cannot keep making life this difficult for itself. The Eagles went 11-of-18 on third down, which is an absurd 61.1% conversion rate. That’s why they sustained drives despite averaging only 4.7 yards per play, turning the ball over twice and rushing for 89 yards on 32 attempts. Winning on third down is obviously good. Needing Hurts to repeatedly deliver elite throws on third-and-long isn’t a sustainable offensive identity. The early-down numbers are wild. I mean, come on…

Chicago Bears Injury News: Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol – Windy City Gridiron

If Williams and Bagent can’t go, look for 38-year-old Case Keenum to get the start. Keenum last played in a regular-season game on Christmas Eve, 2023, when he started for the Houston Texans. He was 11 of 17 for 62 yards and 2 interceptions before giving way to Davis Mills in the fourth quarter. Chicago also has undrafted free agent Miller Moss on the practice squad, who would likely be elevated to back up Keenum.

Game Review – PHI 24, TEN 20 – Iggles Blitz

All the WRs contributed in this game. Dontayvion Wicks went 5-74, with several catches coming on 3rd or 4th down. He did a good job of getting open and catching the ball when it came his way. He had a drop on the final drive, but it was only going to be for a couple of yards so the team was better off that he didn’t catch that. Darius Cooper was 2-26 and caught the game-winning TD. He had a chance for another good gain, but the pass was just a bit too far out front. Hollywood Brown had 2 runs for 12 yards. Makai Lemon caught 1 pass for 14 yards. He also had 1 run for -5 yards, a pass behind the LOS. Really good game from the WR corps.

The Winners and Losers of the NFL Week 2 – The Ringer

Every Eagles game becomes a national referendum on how much credit belongs to Hurts and how much belongs to everything surrounding him. But right now, there are real problems for Philadelphia to solve. The offensive line hasn’t played well in the first two weeks. The early-down offense has created far too many difficult third-down situations. Vic Fangio’s defense has struggled throughout both second halves and allowed Cam Ward to play one of the best games of his career on Sunday. But after an offseason spent discussing how much talent the Eagles have assembled around their quarterback, they are 2-0 because of him. He was the one who finished that shit, and he got to tell that to Simmons’s face.

Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams – ESPN

The early surprise: The defense has generated zero takeaways. The verdict: Mirage. The Eagles ranked sixth in opponent turnovers (47) over the past two seasons under defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, and they should see their fortunes turn in the near future. They’ll get a boost in the pass-rushing department when their splash offseason acquisition, Jonathan Greenard, returns from his pec injury. “Super, super close,” Greenard said last week. Do-it-all defensive back Cooper DeJean has been dealing with calf and abdomen injuries, as well; the healthier he gets, the more dangerous that back end becomes.

Does Zach Ertz still have the juice to contribute to the Eagles? Here’s what the film — and history — says – Inquirer

While Ertz still can thrive as a receiver, he does not bring much as a blocker, an area where the Eagles have struggled through two weeks. Much of his time in Washington was spent as a detached slot receiver on run-pass option plays or as a lead blocker on the perimeter for zone-read runs with Jayden Daniels. He has not had an in-line blocking role for the majority of his career, and that is unlikely to change in this reunion. But with Goedert missing time, Ertz’s contributions as a pass catcher seemed to be what the Eagles are seeking in the franchise legend.

10 reasons to be optimistic about the Eagles’ defense – NBCSP

Pass defense: Not everything has gone well so far, but the Eagles’ pass defense has been elite. The Eagles have only allowed 166 passing yards per game, 4th-fewest in the league, and they’ve held opposing quarterbacks to 57.4 percent completion percentage, also 4th-lowest in the league. They’ve only allowed two passing touchdowns, tied for 6th-fewest in the league. And they’ve allowed only six total plays of 20 yards or more, 10th-fewest in the league through two games. This is a passing league and the Eagles are built to stop the pass.

2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Falcons rise, Patriots tumble following injury – PFF

4) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. The injury to Landon Dickerson forced some shuffling on the Eagles’ offensive line, with Cam Jurgens moving from center to left guard and Drew Kendall coming in to replace him in the middle of the offensive line. The results weren’t great for either player, with both earning sub-50.0 PFF grades against the Tennessee Titans. Lane Johnson was the team’s best pass-blocker, producing a 97.7% PFF pass-block win rate. There is clearly still a lot of talent on this offensive line, but how Jurgens and Kendall perform this week will be key.

Spadaro: Jalen Hurts, Eagles do what it takes to win – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

This has been, as all parties said from the very start, a collaborative project. Sean Mannion was hired as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator and brought with him a new scheme that required everyone to buy in, make progress on a daily basis, and understand the “why” in his approach. It wasn’t just about Mannion and quarterback Jalen Hurts, although the two understood the importance of “great communication,” as Mannion said, and being “joined at the hip,” as Hurts said. It was about the new-look wide receiver room working together to create a dynamic passing game, the offensive line learning a new approach up front with coach Chris Kuper, the tight ends and running backs knowing that they would play a large part in the creativity and execution of the vision created by Mannion and Head Coach Nick Sirianni, who said often that the Eagles would continue to incorporate “what worked well for us in the past.” It was a process, and the Eagles introduced it slowly and steadily to the players, so that by the time the world of Eagles fans first heard from Mannion, a strong bond had been made and improvement was visible to the team.

Eagles tailgating: What to know about new parking rules coming for oversized vehicles outside Linc – 6ABC

Tailgating is a Philadelphia tradition, but fans who bring an RV, bus or trailer to Eagles games will soon face new parking rules and higher costs. The Sports Complex Parking Venture is changing its oversized vehicle parking policy beginning Oct. 4, when the Eagles host the Los Angeles Rams. The changes apply only to Eagles home games. Under the new policy, oversized vehicles will be directed to designated parking areas by lot attendants outside Lincoln Financial Field. Those areas will be in Lot D and the upper section of Lot N.

Falcons poach CB Robert Longerbeam from Eagles practice squad – The Falcoholic

Longerbeam is unlikely to play much in Week 3, but gives Atlanta a developmental option with some real upside. The former Rutgers cornerback was a playmaker in college who flashed real coverage skills and boasts quality physicality, but isn’t the biggest corner and missed all of the 2025 season with an injury after the Ravens drafted him in the sixth round in the 2025 NFL Draft. Baltimore risked waiving him after a quality summer and lost him to the Eagles, and now the Falcons will get a closer look at him.

    Jaxson Dart injury: NY Giants’ QB could miss the remainder of the 2026 season – Big Blue View

    The Giants were looking like a potential playoff contender after Dart completed 23 of 29 for 230 yards and 3 touchdowns while also running 11 times for 54 yards in a season-opening 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. Now, the Giants are looking at having Jameis Winston at quarterback for the remainder of the season. The Giants have quarterback Jake Haener on their practice. They could bring back Brandon Allen, who was let go when rosters were trimmed to 53 players, as a third quarterback, or look elsewhere.

    Cowboys offense provides fireworks while the defense is still a little leaky – Blogging The Boys

    The defense struggled mightily to bring the quarterback down. The pressure was inconsistent, sometimes getting close, other times allowing the quarterback to have all day. In every instance, they could never quite finish the play with a sack. Even knowing it is a strength of Washington’s offense, the front seven failed to keep the quarterback in the pocket. The QB kept eluding defenders and churning out big gains on the ground. Watching the game closely, there were some instances where Daniels was very decisive and very fast, and sometimes you have to just recognize the other team has great players too, so it wasn’t as egregious as it initially appeared. It’s still something to be mindful of. While last week the defense was burned by designed runs, on Sunday it came from pure improvisation because the defense was not equipped to make stops in space. The good news is the team will be moving to a stretch of games against quarterbacks with far less mobility soon. The bad news is they have Lamar Jackson coming up next, so it might get a little worse before it gets better.

    What Washington Commanders will get from Marcus Mariota – Hogs Haven

    The Commanders can be a functional and winning football team with Mariota. As he said after the loss to Dallas, he can work with this scheme. “With as much experience as I’ve had, I feel comfortable,” Mariota told on-site reporters. “We’ve got a great crew. Those guys didn’t blink at all, and I thought we did a good job of moving the ball in the second half. But yeah, I feel confident. I feel comfortable. I really like what Coach Blough is doing. I believe in this system and we’ll get this thing right.” Washington needs to stack some victories and do it now after starting 0-2 on the season and within the division. We’ll see when Daniels can return. The Commanders must hold serve until he does. A lot of the responsibility for that falls on Mariota, someone we all know well and someone we know can be a functional quarterback and produce wins that the Commanders need. Desperately.

    Ranking NFL’s 0-2 teams by chances to actually make the playoffs – SB Nation

    6) Washington Commanders. It was tough to watch Jayden Daniels dislocate his left elbow again in Sunday’s loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Dan Quinn said the team will rally around backup Marcus Mariota, and the veteran does give Washington a fighting chance each week. But with games coming up against Seattle, Indianapolis, the Giants, San Francisco, Philadelphia, and the Rams, Daniels going down comes ahead of a rather tough stretch of games. Maybe Washington steals a game or two, but even that would mean overcoming a 2-6 start which seems like too high of a hill to climb.

    Colts Worked Out Three WRs Including Quez Watkins – NFL Trade Rumors

    Quez Watkins, 28, is a former sixth-round pick by the Eagles in the 2020 NFL Draft out of Southern Mississippi. He finished out the final year of his four-year, $3.5 million contract with the Eagles.

    Detroit Lions poach rookie safety off Steelers practice squad – Pride Of Detroit

    The Detroit Lions have signed defensive back Bishop Fitzgerald off of the Pittsburgh Steelers practice squad and onto their 53-man roster. To make move for the Fitzgerald, the Lions have released [former Eagles] veteran linebacker Joe Bachie. Lions coach Dan Campbell telegraphed this move on Monday, noting that the team needed both a shakeup in the secondary and some help at safety after Avonte Maddox suffered a season-ending foot injury [Note: Maddox is now officially on IR]. item.title: UFL announces homes of two relocated franchises for 2027 season
item.description: The UFL is bringing spring football to Colorado and Rhode Island in 2027 after relocating the Birmingham Stallions and Houston Gamblers.
item.content:encoded:
The United Football League (UFL) is moving to two new markets ahead of its 2027 and is planning to expand to another in 2028 as it continues to undergo major changes under the leadership of Mike Repole.

The UFL's new franchises for 2027 will be located in Colorado Springs, Colorado and Pawtucket, Rhode Island. In 2028, the league will be adding a team in Utah. The franchise will join the UFL alongside an Oklahoma City franchise, which was previously announced as an expansion team in April 2026.

Nicknames for the franchises have not yet been revealed. The two new teams for 2027 will replace the Birmingham Stallions and Houston Gamblers, who the league originally announced would be relocated on July 30.

The UFL did not immediately provide information about which franchises would relocate to each city. It was also not immediately clear whether staff and players would be retained as part of the relocation process or whether the UFL would redistribute players ahead of its 2027 season.

The UFL has now announced expansion to two new markets while relocating five of its franchises since Repole joined its ownership group. Last offseason, the league added the Columbus Aviators, Louisville Kings and Orlando Storm at the expense of the Memphis Showboats, Michigan Panthers and San Antonio Brahmas.

The goal of these relocations? Repole has focused primarily on finding the right venues, placing a strong emphasis on finding smaller-sized stadiums that will create a better game-day experience for fans and an improved broadcast for the league's partners at Fox and ESPN.

"Even though the stadium is smaller, the platform will be bigger because it's going to be a sold-out stadium," Repole told USA TODAY Sports in an October 2025 interview.

Additionally, the UFL's press release announcing the new franchises highlighted they would "expand the league’s geographic footprint" and build on the "momentum" the league is generating.

"2026 was an incredible year for the UFL, and seeing the response from our fans, players, and partners has made what comes next even more exciting," Repole said in the press release. "There is a real energy around this league right now, and we’re thrilled to bring that energy to four new markets.

"We said in July that our next step was finding the right markets, venues, and fan bases where we can work with local leaders to build the strongest franchises for today and for the future, and we believe Colorado, Rhode Island, Oklahoma, and Utah represent those qualities. We’re thankful to the local leaders and partners who believed in this vision and have helped us get here. We can’t wait to see these markets come to life and the best part is that this is just the beginning."

Here's more to know about the UFL's relocations, as well as the league's plan for eventual expansion.

What to know about the UFL's Rhode Island franchise

The UFL's Rhode Island franchise is slated to play in Pawtucket. The city is best known for hosting the Boston Red Sox's Triple-A affiliate from 1973 to 2020, before the team relocated to Worcester, Massachusetts.

The Rhode Island UFL team will play at Centreville Bank Stadium, which opened in 2025 and is also home to Rhode Island FC of the United Soccer League (USL). Centreville Bank Stadium has a capacity of 10,500, helping it fit Repole's vision of the UFL playing at smaller-sized stadiums.

Paul Byrne, the general manager of Centreville Bank Stadium, expressed excitement about being able to welcome professional football to Pawtucket.

"There is tremendous energy around sports in the Ocean State, and we’re proud to continue establishing Centreville Bank Stadium as a premier destination for major sporting and entertainment events," Byrne said. "Bringing professional football to Pawtucket is another exciting milestone for our venue and for Rhode Island, and our team can’t wait to welcome fans from across the state and deliver an unforgettable game-day experience."

The UFL is slated to announce the Rhode Island team's nickname, branding, logo and more at a public event on Oct. 18 at Centreville Bank Stadium. The team will make its home debut in Week 2 of the 2027 UFL season on Friday, April 2, at 8 p.m. ET.

What to know about the UFL's Colorado franchise

Like the UFL's Rhode Island franchise, the Colorado franchise will be playing at USL stadium. Colorado will play at Weidner Field in Colorado Springs, which is home to the Colorado Springs Switchbacks FC.

Weidner Field opened in 2021 and has a capacity of 8,000. The Colorado franchise will make its debut at the stadium on Sunday, April 11, during Week 3 of the 2027 UFL season.

Colorado Springs mayor Yemi Mobolade referred to the arrival of the UFL in Colorado Springs as "a vote of confidence" in the city.

"A UFL team will put Colorado Springs in front of a national audience, bring fans to Weidner Field, and give southern Colorado a professional football team to call its own," Mobolade said in the UFL's press release. "We are proud to welcome the UFL to the foot of Pikes Peak – America’s Mountain, and we look forward to seeing our community make this team its own."

The UFL will announce the branding and nickname for its Colorado franchise at a public event at Weidner Field on Oct. 25.

UFL teams 2027

The UFL will remain an eight-team league in 2027 before expanding to 10 teams in 2028. Below is a look at the eight teams currently slated to play in the spring football league:

  • Columbus Aviators
  • Dallas Renegades
  • DC Defenders
  • Louisville Kings
  • Orlando Storm
  • St. Louis Battlehawks
  • Colorado franchise
  • Rhode Island franchise

Oklahoma City and Utah will join the league in 2028.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: UFL announces homes of two relocated franchises for 2027 season

item.title: RB Jamaal Williams contacted Detroit Lions about a reunion
item.description: Former Detroit Lions RB Jamaal Williams is trying to make a comeback and has contacted Dan Campbell.
item.content:encoded:
Jamaal Williams was one of the most beloved players for the Detroit Lions during his two-year stint with the team from 2021-22. His energy was palpable, he showed leadership in times of strife, and he was also pretty dang good, rushing for 17 touchdowns in 2022—a franchise high at the time. He left Detroit after a free agency contract dispute, and his career fizzled away after two unsuccessful years with the New Orleans Saints.

Williams has been out of football since the end of the 2024 season, but he wants back, and he’s been keeping in shape to do so. Apparently he is very much interested in a reunion in Detroit, despite a slightly messy divorce in 2023. Williams told the Detroit Free Press this past weekend that he called Lions coach Dan Campbell about a possible return to Detroit. Campbell responded that they’d keep the door open, but his services were not needed at this time.

“He reached out to Lions coach Dan Campbell last weekend to let Campbell know he was on the comeback trail,” Dave Birkett wrote. “And while Campbell said the Lions are holding tight at running back for now but would keep him in mind if things change, Williams is hopeful he’ll land a job soon and ready to contribute when he does.”

As for the way things ended in Detroit, Williams doesn’t take it personally.

“I didn’t want to go nowhere. I wanted to be there,” Williams told Birkett. “That’s where I wanted to be, but at the same time it’s just like, ‘We just got done having this crazy season, what am I doing that you don’t think I deserve?’ And they had their right, they have their things and it’s cool. And then at the time, it was just the Saints who offered what I wanted. They gave it to me and I ended up there. And that’s pretty much it. There’s no personal feelings, no hard feelings.”

The Lions are down their RB2 with Isiah Pacheco sidelined indefinitely after going through back surgery recently. Reports suggest Pacheco won’t be back until December at the earliest, potentially leaving a power back role for someone like Williams.

However, the Lions have increased the workload of Jahmyr Gibbs, which has severely lessened the role of backup running back in Detroit. Through two weeks, Gibbs’ is currently tied with Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker for the most touches in the NFL (56).

Beyond that, the Lions have shown a lot of faith in 2024 fourth-round pick Sione Vaki to pick up the slack. Though he only has three rushes and two catches, Vaki has played 33 offensive snaps, providing Gibbs with some rest and the Lions offense with a decent pass protector. Detroit also has Jacob Saylors, a strong special teamer who proved he has some rushing skills when he led the NFL in rushing yards this preseason.

As Campbell told Williams, their situation could certainly change. But, for now, it looks like any hope for a reunion between the Lions and Williams is not in the cards.

item.title: NFLSU rookie check-in: Week 3 preview
item.description: How did the rookies do in Week 2?
item.content:encoded:
Another up-and-down week from the LSU rookies.

CB Mansoor Delane

Delane was active for the Chiefs’ Sunday Night Football matchup but didn’t play. That was probably for the best after his injury last week, and he may be able to return against the Dolphins.

Safety A.J. Haulcy

Speaking of that Monday matchup, the Chiefs played the Colts, and this was a big game for A.J. Haulcy. He had a great hit in the game, but the struggles he showed against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1 showed up again. Haulcy was missing tackles consistently, and it took him off the field.

The Texans in Week 3 will be yet another tough matchup for the Colts, and Haulcy will need to do better for this defense.

WR Zavion Thomas

Another week with Thomas not getting into the offense and staying on special teams. For now, that’s the case, especially with Caleb Williams dealing with an injury.

TE Bauer Sharp

Like Thomas, Sharp’s involvement in the offense is extremely limited, and the Bucs are using him as a blocker. With this team struggling at the start of the season, we could see Sharp’s snaps rise over time.

WR Barion Brown

After a disappointing Week 1, Brown had one of the plays of the game in Week 2. He wasn’t involved with the offense, but on special teams, Brown had a really great return right before halftime, leading to the Saints scoring a field goal. That return helped the Saints complete their comeback.

In Week 3, expect another special teams day from Brown.

LB Harold Perkins

In an absolutely horrible Falcons game, Perkins still made plays and did well. Out of this entire LSU class, Perkins has been arguably the best of the bunch and is inching closer to having an even bigger role in the Falcons’ defense.

Atlanta will be playing the Packers this week, and with their offensive struggles, Perkins could have another huge game.

QB Garrett Nussmeier

Did not play because Patrick Mahomes is healthy.

EDGE Jack Pyburn

Was inactive for the Chiefs.

The Daily Slop – 23 September 2026

Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!
